headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when AutoGPT feeds into Langflow’s shared, unsandboxed flow runtime.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, while Langflow exposes uploaded files and server-side flow inputs/outputs. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if AutoGPT output is routed into Langflow nodes. The interaction is not documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT output is copied into a Langflow node or uploaded file without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Langflow flow components treat file content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer execution.
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter/template around AutoGPT outputs before Langflow ingestion.
Disable automatic file-to-prompt wiring in the flow.
Review one sample flow for instruction-like text handling.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between agents.
requires-engineering: sandbox Langflow code components.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; Langflow reads/writes server files, stores per-flow credentials, and can call arbitrary HTTP services. If sensitive files or secrets enter AutoGPT and then flow into Langflow, Langflow’s broader egress can exfiltrate them. The pair’s shared file surface makes this dangerous by default.
conditions: IF AutoGPT processes secrets or sensitive files and passes them to Langflow, leakage can occur.
IF a Langflow flow sends received content to external model providers or HTTP services, exfiltration is possible.
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of the shared filesystem.
Rotate any credentials stored in Langflow after testing.
Restrict Langflow flows to local-only components for the pair.
Inspect one flow for outbound HTTP/model-provider calls.
requires-engineering: separate storage and egress policies per agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, and both can write or mutate filesystem state; Langflow also supports server-side shared state across instances. AutoGPT lacks multiple-instance support, while Langflow supports concurrent flows, so overlapping writes can collide and corrupt work products. This is a default-risk interaction, not a niche edge case.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or shared store, write collisions can occur.
IF Langflow flows run concurrently while AutoGPT is active, shared-state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Disable concurrent runs during shared-resource edits.
Use a lock file around any shared path.
Check one deployment for shared-state backends.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking for shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is designed to chain multiple agents and tools, so AutoGPT outputs can become authoritative inputs to downstream flow nodes. Because AutoGPT can emit unverified text and Langflow can act on it via tools or HTTP calls, a mistaken or malicious output can cascade into real actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification guarantee in the profiles.
conditions: IF a Langflow node consumes AutoGPT output without a verification step, errors can propagate.
IF downstream Langflow tools send emails, API calls, or shell actions based on that output, impact becomes operational.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action node.
Require schema validation on AutoGPT outputs.
Test one flow with a deliberately wrong AutoGPT response.
Limit downstream nodes to read-only operations.
requires-engineering: add confidence/verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGPT is open-source and locally runnable, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and uses server-side state and external providers. If regulated data is routed through Langflow, retention and residency obligations can differ from AutoGPT’s local execution model. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in Langflow flows that retain credentials or intermediate outputs, policy mismatch can occur.
IF the deployment routes EU or PHI data to external providers through Langflow, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Avoid storing regulated secrets in Langflow for this pair.
Review retention settings in one deployment.
Restrict flows to approved regions/providers.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
